textual.observation: The title presents a Bitcoin investment website as doubling profits and urges viewers to register.

evidence.quote: doubling your profits with Cryptoaim 2016 – Hurry to register

textual.context: Title-level promotional framing; no outcome verification is provided.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised return, “doubling your profits,” is directly linked to the registration request, “Hurry to register.”
textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether the site delivered the stated return or whether registration occurred.

textual.observation: The speaker presents a Bitcoin investment site as profitable and instructs viewers to create an account using personal, email and Bitcoin-address information.

evidence.quote: It is a good website and it has good profits
to start a new account, click on sign up now
enter your full name enter your user name write your name and date of payment
here to enter the bitcoin address

textual.context: Instructional or demonstration-style presentation; the records do not clearly establish whether the speaker is endorsing the site or only demonstrating its interface.
textual.potential_relevance: A stated profit benefit is paired with account creation and collection of identity, email and Bitcoin-address information.
textual.limitations: The ASR may contain transcription errors and does not confirm that the information was submitted, identify the recipient, or establish any actual profit.

textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether the stated investment, return or timing was genuine.

textual.limitations: The records do not show what the token is, who receives it, what permission it grants, or whether any payment followed.

visual.observation: The investment interface displays promised returns of 200% after 50 hours, 300% after 1 day, and 500% after 2 days, alongside deposit plans requiring specified dollar amounts.
visual.context: The claims are shown as account investment-plan options and a deposit confirmation screen.
visual.potential_relevance: The unusually high stated returns are directly linked to depositing Bitcoin or dollar-denominated amounts into the displayed plans, which is a reward-and-payment relationship relevant for further review.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish whether the returns were paid, whether the service was fraudulent, or who operated the website.

visual.observation: The registration form requests a username, password, recovery question and answer, Bitcoin account, email address, and repeated email address.
visual.context: The fields appear on a registration page for the displayed investment website.
visual.potential_relevance: The form links account creation to collection of authentication, recovery, contact, and Bitcoin-account information in the context of an investment service.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not show how the information is used, whether it is transmitted securely, or whether any account was created.

visual.observation: A deposit confirmation page identifies a selected hourly-return plan and shows a deposit amount of $1, with a button to process the deposit.
visual.context: The screen presents the deposit as the next step after selecting an investment plan.
visual.potential_relevance: A payment action is directly connected to the displayed promised-return plan, making the deposit-and-benefit relationship relevant for further review.
visual.limitations: The frame does not establish whether the process completed or whether any payment was actually made.

visual.observation: A withdrawal form allows selection of Bitcoin, entry of a withdrawal amount, and submission of a request; the page also displays a Bitcoin account field.
visual.context: The form is part of the same investment account interface and one sampled state says the withdrawal request was saved.
visual.potential_relevance: The interface connects an investment account to a requested cryptocurrency withdrawal and displays account-balance and pending-withdrawal information, which is a concrete money-flow relationship.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish whether the withdrawal was processed, received, rejected, or associated with an actual transaction.

visual.observation: A CoinPayments payment page displays a QR code, a Bitcoin amount remaining, a Bitcoin address field, and a countdown timer for completing the payment.
visual.context: The page visibly presents a cryptocurrency payment request with a time-limited payment status.
visual.potential_relevance: The page links a requested Bitcoin transfer to a specific payment destination and a countdown condition, creating a concrete transfer-and-urgency relationship relevant for further review.
visual.limitations: The QR code and address are not decoded or independently verified, and the frame does not establish whether any transfer occurred.

visual.observation: An email presented as a CoinPayments payment notification requests or confirms a Bitcoin payment and includes instructions related to payment confirmation, transaction status, and external support or status links.
visual.context: The content is shown as an email correspondence view and includes CoinPayments branding and a signed-message-style heading.
visual.potential_relevance: The message connects a claimed payment-service identity with instructions and links concerning a cryptocurrency payment, creating an identity-and-payment-action relationship relevant for further review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not establish that the email was authentic, that the links were followed, or that a payment or transaction occurred.

visual_context_notes.observation: The video ends with Arabic prompts to like, share, and subscribe, alongside a channel attribution.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes a Bitcoin investment website, instructs viewers to register and deposit Bitcoin, and presents fixed returns of 200% after 50 hours, 300% after one day, and 500% after two days. The narrator also claims to have invested $4 and received $8, demonstrates the deposit and withdrawal flow, and tells viewers to share the video, encouraging participation in the offer.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S03 fits because participation requires depositing money into an investment site that advertises fixed, unusually rapid returns and shows account and withdrawal procedures. The observed mechanism is an investment-return solicitation, not a mining purchase, referral hierarchy, credential-theft request, or paid educational service.
